claims.text: Controlled phase coexistence can enhance magnetocaloric performance.
Narrowing the distribution of magnetic exchange energies enhances the magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
The proposed microstructural optimization preserves rapid heat transfer, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability.
The untreated NiFeCoCr-based baseline has a mixture of phases and a broad distribution of exchange interactions.
Heat treatment and Pd addition reduce the distribution of exchange energies and produce a more magnetically homogeneous NiFeCoCr-based alloy.
Heat treatment and Pd concentration adjustment promote more uniform coexistence of stable and metastable phases in NiFeCoCr-based alloys.
The critical magnetic transition temperature of the NiFeCoCrPdx family is tunable from about 100 K to above room temperature.
Applied fields below 1 T are relevant to magnetic-refrigeration cycles.
An optimized ratio of metastable and stable crystal phases minimizes the spread of exchange interactions.
Reducing microstructural randomness narrows the distribution of magnetic exchange energies.
A narrower distribution of exchange energies causes more cooperative reordering of magnetic moments at low fields.
More cooperative magnetic reordering increases the magnetic entropy change at low applied fields.
Narrowing exchange-energy variability ensures rapid heat exchange, minimal hysteresis, and retention of mechanical integrity.
The treated alloy will exhibit more than a 30% increase in peak magnetic entropy change below 1 T relative to the untreated alloy.
Treatment will reduce magnetic hysteresis relative to the untreated baseline.
Treatment will maintain or improve thermal conductivity relative to the untreated baseline.
Treatment will maintain or improve mechanical strength relative to the untreated baseline.
NiFeCoCrPdx alloys undergo second-order magnetic phase transitions.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to alloys with different transition orders or with non-transition-metal constituents.
